changed: Dances you import from The Caller's Box read a neighbor number before the men or the women as a figure instead of text. When two men or two women do the figure together, it names which pair meets: "N2 Men allemande left 3/4" is the next larks (in your dialect's words) allemanding, and "N0 Women swing" the previous robins swinging. When the men or women act by themselves, such as "N2 Men turn alone", it is all the larks, and the number is kept as a note. When the figure is done with a neighbor, the number names the neighbor: "N2 Men roll away neighbor" has the larks roll away their next neighbors. Otherwise, such as "N3 Men allemande" or a figure done with partners, the number is kept as a note. A figure that ends in the number instead, such as "Men allemande left 3/4 [with N2]", reads the same way.

Dances you import from The Caller's Box read a hey whose passes name same-role neighbors (SRN) as a hey, and keep "with hands" or a trailing "[with N1]" on a hey as a note instead of leaving the line as text.
Dances you import from The Caller's Box read "Pass the ocean (to wave of four (NR,WL))" as a pass the ocean into that wave.

The Caller's Box figure dialect reads a neighbour number before a role pair (`N2 role1s …`) as the role among those neighbours (`nextRole1s`, `prevRole2s`) when the pair does the figure together (a fixed list of pair moves: swing, allemande, do si do, chain and the like), as the numbered neighbours in `whom` or `who2` when the figure is done with a neighbour, and otherwise as the role pair with a `with` note; a role-pair clause ending in a lone `[with N0]`–`[with N4]` reads the same way. It also decodes `SRN` (same-role neighbours) in hey pass lists and keeps `with hands` and a trailing `[with …]` as the hey's note, and reads a nested wave annotation on pass the ocean.
